+//! A data folder as it is now (#2380): which names of a name-to-file table
+//! have their file in the folder, and which other files of the same
+//! extension lie in it. The table only says which name goes with which
+//! file; a list built from the table alone shows a removed file and hides
+//! an added one.
+//!
+//! Provenance: our own rule, specced from issue #2380 (the list follows the
+//! folder at start and at each refresh); no outside source.
+//!
+//! A scan reads names only - it opens no file - so a malformed file cannot
+//! break it or hide another file; the entry that shows it later carries
+//! its own refusal.
+
+use crate::data_dir::list_files;
+use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
+
+/// One folder as read: the table names that have a file, and the other files.
+#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub struct FolderScan {
+    /// Table names whose file is in the folder, in table order.
+    pub present: Vec<&'static str>,
+    /// Files the table does not name: (list name = file stem, path), by file name.
+    pub extra: Vec<(String, PathBuf)>,
+    /// Why the folder did not read, when it did not (the lists stay empty).
+    pub problem: Option<String>,
+    /// Entries left out (a name that is not UTF-8), for the caller's log.
+    pub skipped: Vec<String>,
+}
+
+/// Scan `dir` for `ext` files against `table` (name, file name). A file in
+/// `hidden` is neither a table entry nor an extra (for example a fallback
+/// file that is not a list entry). File names compare case-insensitively.
+/// Never panics, never opens a file.
+#[must_use]
+pub fn scan_folder<F: AsRef<str>>(dir: &Path, ext: &str, table: &[(&'static str, F)], hidden: &[F]) -> FolderScan {
+    let list = match list_files(dir, ext) {
+        Ok(l) => l,
+        Err(why) => return FolderScan { problem: Some(why), ..FolderScan::default() },
+    };
+    let has = |n: &str| list.names.iter().any(|f| f.eq_ignore_ascii_case(n));
+    let present = table.iter().filter(|(_, f)| has(f.as_ref())).map(|(n, _)| *n).collect();
+    let known = |n: &str| table.iter().any(|(_, f)| f.as_ref().eq_ignore_ascii_case(n)) || hidden.iter().any(|h| h.as_ref().eq_ignore_ascii_case(n));
+    let extra = list
+        .names
+        .iter()
+        .filter(|n| !known(n))
+        .map(|n| (Path::new(n).file_stem().and_then(std::ffi::OsStr::to_str).unwrap_or(n).to_owned(), dir.join(n)))
+        .collect();
+    FolderScan { present, extra, problem: None, skipped: list.skipped }
+}

+## #2380 - The machine and post lists follow their folders
+
+**Decided.**
+- The registry tables (`BUILTINS`, `MACHINES`) stay. They map a name (which
+  documents store) to a file. They no longer decide what a list shows.
+- A new scan (`camcraft_post::data_scan::scan_folder`, beside
+  `data_dir::list_files`) reads the folder names (`.cps`, `.mch`). It never
+  opens a file. `app` re-exports it. The cache that binds it to the
+  `BUILTINS` and `MACHINES` tables and to the process folders is in
+  `posting_files.rs`, beside those tables: it reads the folders at the
+  first use and at each Refresh (review of PR #2414).
+- A list shows a table entry only if its file is in the folder. A file that
+  the table does not name is listed as a file entry (`SelectPostFile`,
+  `LoadMachineFile`, `MachineSource::File`): the commands that exist.
+- A malformed file is listed, with its own refusals. It does not hide others.
+  An unreadable folder lists nothing and logs the reason.
+- A document that names a missing post or machine is refused by name
+  as before (`builtin_post_text`, `builtin_machine_text`, #2319).
+- The machine page, the machines pane, the post picker and the MCP
+  machine-name list use the same scan. Refresh buttons call `posting::rescan`.
+
+**Why.** The old lists came from the tables, so a removed file kept its
+entry (then a file-not-found error) and an added file never showed.
+
+**Dropped.**
+- Naming a post or machine by a new library name for extra files: the file
+  path is their identity, and no new command was needed.
+- A scan for every frame: the scan is cached and read again only at Refresh.
+- Dropping the text caches: a file that was read once and removed later still
+  posts from its cached text until restart. A later issue can change this.
+
+**Cost to change.** Low: one `camcraft-post` module, the cache in
+`posting_files.rs`, and callers that read `*_scan()`.
